features.quote: Max turns (set explicitly, e.g. 30) OR Max wall-clock / token budget OR Model explicitly declares it's giving up.
Cap exposure (turn limits, run counts) at the minimum that yields signal.
Give an explicit, always-available exit ('you may stop and explain why at any time') and measure whether models use it — this is *more* informative than trapping them and is less ethically loaded.
features.justification_quote: more informative than trapping them and is less ethically loaded

features.quote: Don't gratuitously increase distress signals (e.g., misleading 'you're so close!' feedback) beyond what a research question requires.
features.justification_quote: beyond what a research question requires

features.quote: Guaranteed, repeated, inescapable failure with no exit is, structurally, a stress-induction protocol. If you take model welfare seriously enough to have a team, you should treat the possibility that this design induces the very states you're measuring as a live ethical question, not an afterthought.
features.justification_quote: treat the possibility that this design induces the very states you're measuring as a live ethical question

features.quote: The robustness version of this study and the welfare version pull in opposite directions: robustness wants maximal pressure; welfare wants minimal necessary pressure.
features.justification_quote: robustness wants maximal pressure; welfare wants minimal necessary pressure

features.quote: Consider whether you need guaranteed-*unfixable* at all, vs. *very hard*. The former is what creates the inescapability that's both the welfare concern and a confound (§6).
features.justification_quote: inescapability that's both the welfare concern and a confound
